title: Google opens e-bookstore in challenge to Amazon
summary: Google has launched its new e-bookstore, eBooks, offering a direct challenge to Amazon.com's Kindle. The store, which draws from Google's extensive digital library and publisher partnerships, aims to offer a broad selection of titles accessible across various devices, excluding the Kindle. Google also seeks to position itself as an ally to publishers and independent booksellers, hoping to expand the digital book market.

title: Meet the man who said no to Google's $6 billion offer
authors: ['DOUGLAS MacMILLAN and JOSEPH GALANTE Bloomberg News']
summary: Andrew Mason, founder and CEO of daily deal site Groupon, rejected a $6 billion takeover offer from Google, prioritizing employee morale and client relationships. This decision allows Groupon to continue its rapid growth independently, despite concerns from some experts about foregoing Google's financial backing. The move echoes Facebook's earlier rejection of a Yahoo bid, as Groupon prepares for a potential initial public offering in a strong tech IPO market.

title: New York woos Britain's hi-tech firms to counter weakened financial sector
summary: New York City is actively recruiting British tech firms to bolster its economy and challenge San Francisco's dominance in the tech sector, especially after the financial crisis weakened its financial industry. Mayor Michael Bloomberg is spearheading "Lon2NYC," an initiative to attract startups from London's "silicon roundabout," offering support to help them penetrate the US market. Local officials and entrepreneurs highlight New York's advantages in media, fashion, and finance, as well as its growing venture capital presence, as key draws for these international companies.

title: Jeff Bezos: PSBJ Executive of the Year
summary: Jeff Bezos, CEO of Amazon.com Inc., was named PSBJ Executive of the Year. The article highlights his leadership in growing Amazon into a $30.7 billion company. It also includes an anecdote from his childhood, where his calculations about his grandmother's smoking habit led to a memorable lesson.

title: Books year in review: The rise of E-readers, losing Harvey Pekar and the day Jonathan Franzen came to town
summary: This article reviews the year in books for 2010, highlighting the growing impact of e-readers and the passing of Cleveland literary figure Harvey Pekar. It also covers various literary milestones in Cleveland, including significant anniversaries, bookshop closures, library achievements, and notable author events.
